name: LMC555CMMX_NOPB
title: LMC555 CMOS timer, 1.5 V to 15 V, in SOIC, VSSOP, PDIP and DSBGA
summary: A CMOS member of the 555 timer family: one RC network sets a one-shot pulse width, or two resistors and one capacitor set an oscillator's frequency and duty cycle. It runs from 1.5 V to 15 V on about 130 to 220 µA typical, its inputs draw picoamps, and it oscillates up to 3 MHz. The SOIC, VSSOP and PDIP parts keep the standard 555 pinout; an 8-bump DSBGA is also offered. LMC555CMMX/NOPB is the commercial-temperature (-40 °C to 85 °C) VSSOP-8 part on a 3500-piece reel, marked ZC5.

pins.name: TRIGGER
pins.function: Active-low trigger. Pulling it below 1/3 V+ sets the internal flip-flop: OUTPUT goes high and the short across the timing capacitor is released.

pins.name: OUTPUT
pins.function: Timer output. Its low level is tested at up to 50 mA sink and its high level at up to 10 mA source.

pins.name: RESET
pins.function: Active-low reset. A low pulse ends a timing cycle and holds OUTPUT low; it takes priority over TRIGGER and THRESHOLD. Tie it to V+ when it is not used, so it cannot cause false triggering.

pins.name: CONTROL VOLTAGE

curves.title: TRIGGER, capacitor voltage, and OUTPUT waveforms in monostable mode
curves.conditions: Monostable LED flasher circuit, time delay 5.17 s

circuits.title: Monostable (one-shot)
circuits.description: One-shot timer. While idle, DISCHARGE holds C empty and OUTPUT is low. A low-going pulse on TRIGGER sets the flip-flop; OUTPUT goes high and C charges through RA until THRESHOLD reaches 2/3 VS, about 1.1 RA C later, when OUTPUT drops and C is dumped again. Both the charging and the threshold scale with VS, so the pulse length does not depend on the supply. The same circuit, driven by a pulse train with its timing set longer than the input period, divides the input frequency.
notes: Pulse width tH = 1.1 RA C.
Typical waveforms: VS = 5 V, RA = 9.1 kΩ, C = 0.01 µF; input and output 5 V/div, capacitor 2 V/div, 0.1 ms/div.
As a frequency divider, the example divides by three.

circuits.title: Astable (variable duty cycle oscillator)
circuits.description: Free-running multivibrator. TRIGGER and THRESHOLD are tied together on the timing capacitor, which fills through the series pair RA, RB and empties through RB alone into DISCHARGE, swinging between 1/3 VS and 2/3 VS. OUTPUT is high while C charges and low while it discharges, so the RA:RB ratio sets the duty cycle; the frequency does not depend on the supply.
notes: High time 0.693 (RA + RB) C, low time 0.693 RB C, frequency 1.44 / ((RA + 2RB) C).
Typical waveforms: VS = 5 V, RA = 1.78 kΩ, RB = 4.12 kΩ, C = 0.01 µF; output 5 V/div, capacitor 1 V/div, 20 µs/div.

circuits.title: Monostable LED flasher
circuits.description: A push-button one-shot that lights an LED for about five seconds. TRIGGER is pulled up to VCC by 10 kΩ and grounded by the button; pressing it starts a cycle. The 10 kΩ and 470 µF timing pair gives 1.1 R C = 5.17 s. OUTPUT drives the LED through a 470 Ω series resistor to ground. RESET is unused and tied to the supply; CONTROL VOLTAGE has a 0.01 µF capacitor to ground.
notes: The design procedure works from a 5 s target: R C = 4.545, giving C = 45.4 µF for R = 100 kΩ, rounded to R = 100 kΩ and C = 47 µF. The circuit uses 10 kΩ and 470 µF, the same R C product.
Measured time delay 5.17 s.

circuits.title: Pulse width modulator
circuits.description: The monostable connection triggered by a continuous pulse train on TRIGGER. A signal on CONTROL VOLTAGE moves the threshold level, so each output pulse is lengthened or shortened with the modulating signal.

circuits.title: Pulse position modulator
circuits.description: The astable connection with a modulating signal on CONTROL VOLTAGE. The signal shifts the threshold voltage and with it each timing interval, so the position of the output pulses follows the modulation; a triangle wave is the example signal.

circuits.title: 50% duty cycle oscillator
circuits.description: Square-wave oscillator whose timing capacitor is charged and discharged from OUTPUT through one resistor, RC. TRIGGER and THRESHOLD both sit on C, so it ramps between the two comparator levels through the same resistance each way and the output is high and low for equal times. DISCHARGE, with a pull-up to VS, gives a second output.
notes: Frequency f = 1 / (1.4 RC C).

circuits.title: Test circuit
circuits.description: Characterization fixture. With every switch open it measures the static parameters. Closing S2 and S4 makes a one-shot: 10 kΩ from VS to DISCHARGE and THRESHOLD, 0.1 µF to ground, triggered from the TRIGGER input (the timing-accuracy test, 1.1 ms nominal). Closing S1 and S3 makes an astable: TRIGGER tied to THRESHOLD, 1 kΩ from VS to DISCHARGE, 1 kΩ from DISCHARGE to THRESHOLD and 0.1 µF to ground (the astable-frequency test).

circuits.title: Maximum frequency test circuit
circuits.description: Fixture for the 3 MHz maximum-frequency and output-edge figures: an astable with 470 Ω from VS to DISCHARGE, 200 Ω from DISCHARGE to the joined TRIGGER and THRESHOLD, and 200 pF to ground. OUTPUT goes to a coaxial connector; RESET is held at VS.

equations.name: Monostable pulse width

where.tH: time OUTPUT stays high after a trigger
where.RA: timing resistor from VS to DISCHARGE and THRESHOLD

equations.note: Independent of VS, because charge rate and threshold both scale with it.

where.D: fraction of each period for which OUTPUT is low

where.RC: resistor from OUTPUT to the timing capacitor

operation.text: Three equal 100 kΩ resistors in series from V+ to ground set the comparator references; CONTROL VOLTAGE is the upper tap at 2/3 V+. The THRESHOLD comparator resets an RS flip-flop and the TRIGGER comparator sets it. The flip-flop drives the output buffer and the DISCHARGE transistor, and RESET acts on the flip-flop directly.

Built in TI's LMCMOS process. Dissipation is under 0.2 mW from a 1.5 V supply and under 1 mW from 5 V. Current spikes on the supply during output edges are small, and the RESET, TRIGGER and THRESHOLD inputs draw picoamps (10 pA typical).

Offered in 8-pin SOIC (D), VSSOP (DGK) and PDIP (P), and in an 8-bump chip-scale DSBGA (YPB), about 1.43 mm × 1.41 mm. The SOIC, VSSOP and PDIP versions have the pinout of the NE555, SE555 and LM555, so they drop into existing 555 layouts.

The timing capacitor is held discharged until TRIGGER is pulled below 1/3 VS. That sets the flip-flop, which drives OUTPUT high and releases the capacitor. The capacitor charges exponentially toward VS; at 2/3 VS, after tH = 1.1 RA C, the THRESHOLD comparator resets the flip-flop, OUTPUT goes low and DISCHARGE empties the capacitor. OUTPUT then stays low until the next trigger.

RESET wins over TRIGGER, and TRIGGER wins over THRESHOLD, so a trigger pulse has to be shorter than tH. TRIGGER needs a pulse of at least 20 ns and RESET at least 400 ns. Once a cycle is running, further trigger pulses have no effect provided TRIGGER has returned high 10 µs or more ahead of the interval's end; a low on RESET still ends the cycle early. In monostable use, TRIGGER is returned high before the timing cycle finishes.
Connect RESET to V+ when it is not used, which prevents false triggering. If RESET is used at -20 °C or below, VS has to be 2.0 V or higher.

With TRIGGER and THRESHOLD joined, the timer retriggers itself. Charging current flows through RA in series with RB; discharging current flows through RB alone, and the capacitor cycles between 1/3 VS and 2/3 VS. The duty cycle follows from the RA:RB ratio, and the charge time, discharge time and frequency are independent of VS.

CONTROL VOLTAGE moves the threshold, and so the timing. In monostable mode with a steady trigger train, a signal there varies the output pulse width (pulse width modulation). In astable mode it varies the time delay of each cycle and hence where the pulses fall (pulse position modulation).

A monostable whose timing cycle is longer than the input period ignores the triggers that arrive while OUTPUT is high, so its output is a fraction of the input frequency; the example divides by three.
Runs from 1.5 V to 15 V. Bypass with no less than a 0.1 µF capacitor alongside a 1 µF electrolytic, mounted close to the LMC555 on short traces.

Keep the 0.1 µF and 1 µF bypass pair close to the device and the timing capacitor close to DISCHARGE. Pouring ground over the whole bottom layer helps against noise. The example layout puts the timing resistor R1 and capacitor C1 beside pins 6 and 7, a 0.01 µF capacitor C2 from CONTROL VOLTAGE to ground, a 0.1 µF ceramic C3 and a 1 µF electrolytic C4 across the supply, and RESET tied to V+ when reset is not used.
